articles.headline: Nick Sirianni defended decision to play Saquon Barkley after RB suffered another injury
keyFacts: Eagles running back Saquon Barkley exited Monday's game against the Cowboys after suffering a back injury while playing through a hamstring issue.
Head coach Nick Sirianni defended the medical team's decision to play Barkley, stating the player was on a strict pitch count and heavily monitored.
It remains unconfirmed whether this new injury will force Barkley to miss additional playing time.
body: The past couple weeks haven't exactly been a banner display for the Eagles on the injury front . And on Monday, head coach Nick Sirianni once again found himself answering for the decisions of his medical team.

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley had missed the past two weeks with a hamstring injury and was listed as questionable heading into Monday night's game against the Cowboys. But after just seven carries and two receptions, Barkley exited the game and didn't return.
Though Barkley left with an announced back injury, Sirianni was still asked if he felt the Eagles rushed the star running back to return.
He defended how the Eagles handled the injury to reporters after the game. Via Pro Football Talk :

“Obviously, you saw that he was on a pitch count out there today. There was constant communication to see how he was feeling, see where he was, and obviously, he came out early in the second half. Again, when you go into something like that, you make sure that the player’s health is first and foremost. Is he ready to go? Do they feel ready to go? Do the doctors and trainers feel like they’re ready to go? We felt like that was the case today, but obviously wanted to keep a close eye on him, and he’s tough as heck. He wanted to be out there for his teammates, probably had to slow him [down] as far as -- he’d be out there every play because of the person he is and the teammate he is and the player he is and the toughness that he has.
“So, we tried to be smart with him there, but it was good to have him back out there. He obviously had a nice game and was very productive when he touched the football.”
It did appear that Barkley tweaked the hamstring injury on his first carry of the game. The back injury was a result of him trying to play through it.

Saquon Barkley said it was a compensatory injury to his back. He tweaked his hamstring on his first run of the game and picked up the back injury trying to play through it. #Eagles pic.twitter.com/WJI68W8Dy1
— EJ Smith (@EJSmith94) October 27, 2026 It remains to be seen if this latest injury will keep Barkley sidelined once again.

articles.headline: Fantasy football Week 8 waiver wire: Jonah Coleman, Rachaad White headline must-add running backs
keyFacts: Jonah Coleman and Rachaad White are highlighted as top running back waiver wire additions for Week 8.
Sean Payton told reporters that the Broncos need to get Jonah Coleman more touches moving forward.
Rachaad White has at least three more games as the lead running back while Jacory Croskey-Merritt recovers from a groin injury.
body: Jonah Coleman and Rachaad White should be added in all leagues. Both have the chance to be difference makers in Week 8 and beyond.

Now, you are not going to see them mentioned as running backs to add below because both are rostered in more than 65 percent of leagues on CBS Sports. But we know they are widely available on other platforms, and you should be prepared to spend plenty of your FAAB on each running back.

Coleman (68 percent rostered on CBS Sports), who was on injured reserve due to an ankle injury for four games prior to Week 7, led Denver's running backs with nine carries for 54 yards and added two catches for 15 yards on two targets against Arizona. After the game, Sean Payton told reporters that they "got to get him (Coleman) more touches. Definitely."

That's the tricky part because the Broncos still have J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.  But it's clear watching Coleman -- and knowing Dobbins' injury history -- that it's only a matter of time before Coleman is leading this backfield on a consistent basis.

He is worth adding for at least 25 percent of your remaining FAAB. I would use Coleman as a flex in Week 8 against Kansas City, and he could emerge as a No. 2 Fantasy running back in all leagues if he does well against the Chiefs.

White (72 percent rostered on CBS Sports) was on bye in Week 7, but he has at least three more games as the lead running back for the Commanders with Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve. White should be added in all leagues for at least 20 percent of your remaining FAAB, and he's a borderline starter in all formats in Week 8 against Philadelphia.

In the first game without Croskey-Merritt in Week 6 against San Francisco, White had seven carries for 27 yards and four catches for 30 yards and a touchdown on five targets. He will share touches with Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols until Croskey-Merritt returns to action, but White has the most upside of the trio, especially in PPR. He has scored at least 11.1 PPR points in three of his past four games.

Both of these running backs should be the most coveted players off the waiver wire in Week 8 -- if they are available. And we'll cover plenty of other free agents to add in what should be a busy week on the waiver wire.
We have four teams on a bye (Houston, New Orleans, the Giants and San Francisco) and plenty of injuries. You might have to spend a lot of FAAB to make sure your lineup is ready to go.

Cousins will remain the Raiders' starting quarterback for Week 8, which means he's a low-end Fantasy starter against the Jets. Cousins has scored at least 22.5 Fantasy points in five of his past six games. He should have another solid outing against New York. ... articles.headline: Jaren Jackson Jr. injured against former Grizzlies team, out six weeks
keyFacts: Utah Jazz big man Jaren Jackson Jr. suffered a torn MCL in his right knee against the Memphis Grizzlies.
The team announced on Oct. 27 that Jackson will be re-evaluated in six weeks.
The injury occurred early in the second quarter on Oct. 26 when Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome fell into Jackson's knee.
body: Utah Jazz big man Jaren Jackson Jr. will be re-evaluated in six weeks after suffering a torn MCL in his right knee against the Memphis Grizzlies, the team announced on Oct. 27.

Jackson was injured early in the second quarter on Oct. 26 after Grizzlies guard Ty Jerome drove to the basket, was fouled and fell into Jackson's right knee. Jackson attempted to play through the injury for a couple of possessions before asking to be removed from the game.

Jackson's injury came against the team that drafted him No. 4 overall in the 2018 NBA Draft. He s pent nearly eight seasons with the Grizzlies before being traded to the Jazz on Feb. 3 of last season.
In his time in Memphis, Jackson was a two-time All-Star and the 2022-23 NBA Defensive Player of the Year.
Jackson's injury came in the second meeting this season between the Grizzlies and Jazz. Memphis has won both matchups.
Injuries are creating depth issues in Utah's frontcourt. The team is already without projected starting center Jusuf Nurkic due to a right foot injury.

When Memphis traded Jackson , it acquired three future first-round picks. One of the assets is the most favorable first-round pick between the Utah Jazz, Cleveland Cavaliers and Minnesota Timberwolves in 2027. Utah currently has the worst record of those teams, meaning Memphis would get its pick.

The Grizzlies are off to a 4-0 start for the second time in franchise history and first time since 2014. They'll head to the Moda Center for a matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers on Oct. 29 (9 p.m., CT, DAZN-MEM).
Damichael Cole is the Memphis Grizzlies beat writer for The Commercial Appeal. Contact Damichael at damichael.cole@commercialappeal.com. Follow Damichael on X, formerly known as Twitter, @DamichaelC.

articles.headline: Fleetwood Town v Arsenal: Carabao Cup fourth round – live
keyFacts: Fleetwood Town hosted Arsenal in a Carabao Cup fourth-round match at Highbury Stadium.
The first half was temporarily suspended after a drone hovered over the stadium.
Fleetwood head coach Matt Lawlor stated that the team planned to manage the game with substitutions.
body: 42 mins: Hincapie curls in a tempting cross from the very corner of the penalty area – but it’s not tempting enough for Havertz or Gyokeres to get away from their markers.

37 mins: Fleetwood centre-back Shaun Rooney (no relation) is a big aerial threat – while at St Johnstone, he scored the winner in two Cup finals in the same season. He’s pushing forward whenever the hosts have a chance to get upfield.
34 mins: After a spell of Arsenal possession, O’Neill cuts inside and thwacks it towards the danger area, but Harrison Neal is in place to block it away.
24 mins: Arsenal can’t make anything happen with a scrappy bit of possession in the Fleetwood area, and then Hincapie hoofs a clearance into the car park. Safe to say Arteta’s side haven’t settled.

Marli Salmon won’t want to watch that back; he let Loupalo-Bi get beyond him and his attempted late tackle only pushed the ball further away, allowing the striker to drill it clinically past Meslier. Sweet Carabao!

“Good to see Ceadach O’Neill starting. His two uncles (Paddy & Eoin Bradley) were top class GAA players for Derry,” writes John Brennan. “Eoin was also a top player in the Irish League, winning a few cups along with getting a six-game ban for urinating in Windsor Park during a televised cup semi-final.” Well, that took a turn.
15 mins: THUNK! After nice buildup work from Dowman, Lewis-Skelly goes for a 50-50 with Rooney but the Fleetwood defender prevails, and the thud of the challenge could probably be heard in Blackpool.

The drone has now disappeared, so the referee opts to restart. There are also murky reports of the culprit being apprehended by police. So, it’s back to the game, which will have at least eight minutes added to the first half.

“Who’s the wanker with the drone?” bellow the 5,000-strong home faithful, while the referee talks to Mikel Arteta, Matt Lawlor and various security staff. And now he’s waving the players back to the tunnel!

Arsenal get upfield early on and have a free kick … but play is suspended as the referee, Michael Salisbury, peers up at a distant light in the sky. There’s a drone hovering over Highbury, and it’ll need to be dealt with somehow.
On grounds with the same(ish) name, Tim Gutteridge writes: “I give you Liverpool (Anfield) and Stirling Albion who, until 1993, played their home games at Annfield (with an extra N).”

“The similarities don’t stop there. For much of their history, Stirling Albion played in an all-red strip. And between 1970 and 1973 they were managed by Bob Shankly, the older brother of Liverpool’s Bill.”

The players are out on the pitch, in a fug of firework smoke after some very rapid-fire pyro greeted their arrival. Peter Drury, never knowingly understated, is the Sky commentator and is already talking nights with the stars, marble halls and “two teams galaxies apart”. Let’s go!

“I like to root for the underdog, so fingers crossed the Fishermen of the Cod Army will catch a really big one today!” cheers Peter Oh. It may interest you, Peter, that Fleetwood have a sub called Andy Cannon – surely destined to come on and sink the Gunners.

“‘Arsenal have paid us a lot of respect by naming such a strong team’?Not sure why Matt Lawlor’s being so polite, Arteta’s taking the proverbial Michael with that side. Three kids and a goalie on debut?” writes Dave Estherby. To be fair, one of those kids is Max Dowman, and there are a few first-team regulars in there.

Here’s the Fleetwood head coach, Matt Lawlor: “We’ve had to make changes, with the champions in town. But we’ve got a plan with substitutions to manage the game. Arsenal have paid us a lot of respect by naming such a strong team … it’s a very difficult challenge, but one we should enjoy, and not be overawed.”
“I was just thinking, with the two Highburys – I can only think of the St James(’) Parks (Exeter and Newcastle), but are there any other grounds with very similar names?” asks Shaun T.

“It’s very special, coming to these kinds of grounds – it’s proper English football,” says Mikel Arteta. “In these kinds of conditions, you’re in or you’re out. It’s great to have Marli, Max and Ceadach with us, Ilhan Meslier as well who is making his first appearance for us.” His advice to those young Gunners? “Give me a headache, give me a problem – give me a reason to play you.”

There is one other fourth-round Carabao Cup tie tonight, and it’s an all-League One affair. Bradford City, finalists in 2013,host Robbie Savage’s Peterborough – guaranteeing that at least one third-tier side will make the quarter-finals. Like the match at Highbury, it will go to penalties if still level after 90 minutes – and there’s no VAR.

So, Ilhan Meslier makes his debut in goal for Arsenal, with Christian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie starting as they return from injury; Martin Zubimendi also gets a run-out, while youngsters Max Dowman, Marli Salmon and Ceadach O’Neill all included in Mikel Arteta’s starting XI.

To give everyone a flavour of conditions, it is blowing a gale around the rather quaint Highbury Stadium, almost blowing my laptop onto the pitch. Mikel Arteta will not be too worried about his players adapting to the conditions and will see a front pairing of Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres as integral to killing this game off as soon as possible.

Fleetwood, however, are here to give the Gunners a bloody nose at the very least. They know how to utilise the conditions to their favour and will be straight into the faces of the Premier League champions. They may sit 18th in League Two, but they saw off Sheffield United in the last round and will fancy doing likewise in front of a packed ground.
Some sad news to bring you: Peter Dobing, the captain of Stoke’s 1972 League Cup winning side, has died at the age of 87.

Dobing made 377 appearances over a decade with the Potters and also played for Blackburn and Manchester City. He captained Stoke to glory as they beat Chelsea 2-1 to clinch their first (and only) major trophy, before his playing career was ended by injury just one year later.

Stoke said in a statement: “All at Stoke are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of our ’72 League Cup-winning captain Peter Dobing at the age of 87. The thoughts and sincere condolences of all are with Peter’s friends and family at this immensely difficult time.”

Some Arsenal fans spent years pining for one more game at Highbury Stadium; tonight, they finally get their wish. This particular Highbury is 250 miles northwest of Islington – the home of Fleetwood Town, a team the Gunners have never played before.

While their League Two form could hardly be less remarkable (18th place, with 14 points from 13 games), Fleetwood have picked off Chesterfield, Shrewsbury and second-tier Sheffield United in the Carabao Cup without conceding a goal, earning a last-16 glamour tie against the English champions.

With a trip to Anfield looming on Sunday, Mikel Arteta is expected to give his weariest stars a rest. Young talents like Marli Salmon, Ceadach O’Neill and, yes, Max Dowman are expected to start. They can expect testing conditions at a seaside ground where “the wind goes in all directions”.
Of course, even a depleted and under-experienced Arsenal side will be hot favourites to advance, but this has all the makings of a classic midweek Cup test. Kick-off: 8pm GMT.

articles.headline: Utah officials tie Ted Bundy to 1974 murder of 17-year-old Melissa Smith
keyFacts: Utah officials linked serial killer Ted Bundy to the 1974 murder of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith using DNA profiling, closing the cold case.
The Utah State Crime Lab matched DNA from Smith's body to DNA from another Bundy victim, Laura Aime, officials said.
Investigators said they will continue working to resolve the cold case of Nancy Wilcox, who disappeared in Utah in October 1974.
body: Law enforcement officials in Utah linked the 1974 murder of 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith to serial killer Ted Bundy on Tuesday, closing the cold case of the murder 52 years after her body was found.

Summit County and Salt Lake County investigators led the investigation into the murder since it first opened, but recently partnered with neighboring Utah County after the jurisdiction made developments in a related murder case. After Utah County closed the 1974 murder case of 17-year-old Laura Aime this year, linking it to Bundy using new DNA profiling, the neighboring counties were able to match Bundy’s DNA to the Smith murder.

“The Utah State Crime Lab concluded that the Y-STR DNA profile recovered from Laura Aime’s body matched the Y-STR DNA profile recovered from Melissa Ann Smith’s body. This DNA evidence, when considered alongside evidence related to pattern, motive, means, and opportunity, establishes that Ted Bundy was responsible for Melissa Ann Smith’s murder,” Summit County Attorney Margaret Olson said at the Tuesday press conference.

The closure of the case comes 37 years after Bundy was executed in an electric chair at Florida State Prison for the murder of two students at Florida State University and a 12-year-old girl. He killed at least 30 women and girls before he was sentenced to death. He has been linked to murders in states such as Florida, Utah, Colorado, Idaho, and Washington, according to the Associated Press .

Smith’s body was found on Oct. 27, 1974, by hunters in the Utah forests near the border of Summit County and Salt Lake County. She had been reported missing nine days earlier on Oct. 18, according to the state. She has long been suspected of being a victim of Bundy’s, but investigators never made the connection until Tuesday.

“Today we get to remember Melissa Ann Smith, her family, and all of our victims from cold cases,” Salt Lake County Sheriff Rosie Rivera said during the press conference. “We get the opportunity to show that there is hope out there.”
POLICE ARREST NORTH CAROLINA STATE SENATE CANDIDATE AFTER ARMED STANDOFF

Salt Lake County Sheriff’s Office detective Ben Pender added that the closure of Smith’s case does not “close the book on Ted Bundy,” pointing to the cold case of Nancy Wilcox, who disappeared on Oct. 1, 1974, in Utah.

“Even though, again, the information kind of leads to Ted Bundy, but again we’re not for certain on Nancy Wilcox either,” Pender said. “So we’re going to continue to work that case, and probably in conjunction with Utah County and Summit County as well on that, to see if we can get that resolved as well.”

articles.headline: Magic Is Reprinting a $20 Commander Powerhouse as a Star Trek Fan Favorite
keyFacts: Wizards of the Coast revealed five Star Trek Secret Lair Drops for Magic: The Gathering, featuring reprints inspired by the franchise.
The Lower Decks Drop includes a reprint of the twenty-dollar card Thrasios, Triton Hero reimagined as the character Tendi.
The Set Phasers to Superdrop goes on sale on November 9 at 12 p.m. ET while supplies last.
body: Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek crossover set is only weeks away, and on Tuesday, Wizards of the Coast revealed five new Star Trek Secret Lair Drops featuring reprints inspired by everything from The Wrath of Khan to run-of-the-mill Klingon warriors. A sixth Drop will be revealed later.

The standout, at least for Commander players, is a new Thrasios, Triton Hero, which costs around $20 in its other printings. For the Lower Decks Drop, Thrasios has been reimagined as “Tendi, Exploring the Future,” with art of the enthusiastic Starfleet officer hugging her genetically engineered pet, The Dog. Tendi biologically engineered The Dog in Lower Decks season 1. Though it looks like a normal canine, The Dog can shapeshift, spit lightning, talk, and walk on walls. The flavor text reads, “I did it! I updated the dog!” which is a direct line from Lower Decks.

A green-blue (Simic) legendary merfolk wizard, Thrasios costs one green and one blue mana for a 1/3 creature. Thrasios has a four-cost ability that lets you scry 1, reveal the top card of your library, and then play that card if it’s a land or draw it if it’s not. That makes for a cheap ramp engine that can be fairly explosive in landfall decks, but because it’s not a tap ability, that means you can use the ability as many times as you want as long as you have mana available in multiples of four.

The most useful and flexible thing about Thrasios is the Partner ability that lets you have two Commanders — as long as they both have Partner. That opens up a huge swath of options that allow a deck with Thrasios as the co-Commander to dip into other colors. Tymna the Weaver is a popular option, for example, since that makes the deck the unique white-black-blue-green color scheme commonly referred to as "Witch." But it really depends upon what sort of deck a player wants to build. Regardless, starting with Thrasios as a solid draw engine is a great baseline, and Partner gives you the flexibility to lean in a wide variety of directions.

In the Lower Decks Drop, Tendi is joined by Mariner, Boimler, Rutherford, and the U.S.S. Cerritos. Rutherford is a new version of Silas Renn, Seeker Adept, another card with Partner — which means that diehard Lower Decks fans can build an entire deck with these two friends in the Command Zone.
Here’s a closer look at what’s in each Drop, along with the estimated reprint value of each card pulled from sites like Scryfall based on the cheapest printing.
Secret Lair x Star Trek: Lower Decks
Contents:
- 1x Inti, Seneschal of the Sun as “Mariner, Breaching Protocol” ($1)
- 1x Kambal, Profiteering Mayor as “Boimler, Citing Protocol” ($7)
- 1x Silas Renn, Seeker Adept as “Rutherford, Rebuilding the Past” ($2)
- 1x Thrasios, Triton Hero as “Tendi, Exploring the Future” ($20)
- 1x Weatherlight as “U.S.S. Cerritos, California-Class” ($1)
The Lower Decks Secret Lair is part of the Set Phasers to Superdrop, which goes on sale Nov. 9 at 12 p.m. ET while supplies last. Here’s what else Wizards has revealed so far.
Secret Lair x Star Trek: Beam Me Up

This Drop is a fun fit for blink decks, which focus on effects that temporarily exile creatures and return them to the battlefield, retriggering Enter the Battlefield (ETB) effects. All four cards have reversible art: One side shows a character in danger, and the other shows them safely back in the transporter bay.
Contents:
- 1x Eerie Interlude as “Beam Us Up” ($7)
- 1x Momentary Blink ($0.20)
- 1x Essence Flux as “Materialize” ($1)
- 1x Conjurer’s Closet as “The Transporter” ($3)
Secret Lair x Star Trek: tlhIngan maH

The Klingon-themed Drop features five red cards, including the extra-combat spell Relentless Assault and the mana-generating Seething Song (which is banned in both Historic and Modern). Each card is reversible, with Klingon text on one side and an English translation on the other. War’s Toll is a standout here as one of the meanest red cards ever printed. It’s an enchantment that taps all lands an opponent controls whenever they tap a land for mana, and it forces all of their creatures to attack if even a single creature attacks.
Contents:
- 1x Demand Answers ($0.52)
- 1x Relentless Assault ($2)
- 1x Seething Song ($7)
- 1x War’s Toll ($11)
- 1x Warstorm Surge ($1.50)
Secret Lair x Star Trek: KHAAAAAAAAN

This six-card Drop draws from Star Trek 2: The Wrath of Khan, including a new version of Wrath of the Skies called “Best Served Cold.” (Yes, the extra A’s are part of the official title.) This Drop leans heavily into the flavor of Khan while offering very little in terms of raw card value. That said, this batch of cards is full of neat combat tricks that can find a place in some more niche deck strategies.
Contents:
- 1x Wrath of the Skies as “Best Served Cold” ($2)
- 1x Commandeer ($4)
- 1x Illusionist’s Gambit as “Reliant’s Betrayal” ($0.38)
- 1x Buried Alive ($4)
- 1x Genesis Wave ($0.37)
- 1x Fracture ($0.24)
Secret Lair x Star Trek: New Worlds

Finally, New Worlds turns five basic lands into planets from across the Star Trek universe. The Drop includes two copies of each land, for a total of 10 cards. Fittingly, they’re some of the most gorgeous lands that have been printed in quite some time.
Contents:
- 2x Plains
- 2x Island
- 2x Swamp
- 2x Mountain
- 2x Forest
Wizards also says shoppers will receive one foil copy of Return of the Wildspeaker as “Transporter Boondoggle” for every $199 spent, while supplies last. Orders over $99 ship free.

articles.headline: Re:Build, which spun out Slate Auto, raises $2.1B
keyFacts: Manufacturing accelerator Re:Build announced Tuesday that it has raised $2.1 billion to expand its production capacity and launch new industrial startups.
General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group led the funding round, according to the company.
Re:Build stated that the new capital will be used to manufacture hard tech products in America and help restore U.S. industrial capacity.
body: Re:Build, the Massachusetts-based manufacturing accelerator that spun out EV startup Slate Auto in 2023, has raised $2.1 billion

The company said Tuesday that it will use the funding to “expand Re:Build’s capacity to manufacture hard tech products and launch new industrial startups,” which will “ensure the most innovative products can be made in America for generations to come.” The investment was led by General Catalyst and JPMorganChase’s Strategic Investment Group. Other investors weren’t disclosed.
The funding round comes as increasing attention and capital is flowing to the idea of building up manufacturing and supply chains in the United States, especially as a hedge away from China.

“We started Re:Build because the deindustrialization of America is an economic failure and national security risk,” Re:Build co-founder Jeff Wilke said in a statement. “This capital allows Re:Build to go faster and further than would otherwise be possible, and build a great manufacturing business and a platform for American industrial leadership. The products and companies emerging from our ecosystem prove we can help restore America’s industrial might.”

General Catalyst’s CEO Hemant Taneja echoed those sentiments in a statement saying, “General Catalyst has long believed that rebuilding American industrial capacity is one of the most important economic and national security imperatives of our time.”

Taneja added: “To compete with China, re-industrialize the U.S., and revitalize the towns and jobs that have been left behind, we need platform companies that can operate at genuine scale—and we need our innovation ecosystem to learn how to build hardware again.”

Founded in 2020, Re:Build bills itself as “America’s answer to Shenzhen,” and it has numerous ties to Amazon. It was co-founded by Wilke, who was Amazon’s former commercial CEO. Wei Gao, a longtime Amazon VP and technical adviser to Bezos, is Re:Build’s chief digital and product officer. Multiple other Re:Build executives also worked for the e-commerce giant.

Re:Build claims to have “launched hundreds of products and production systems” over its six-year existence. The company tends to operate two ways. It enters partnerships with industrial companies to “design, engineer, and manufacture products at scale across verticals including aerospace and defense.” It also incubates startups in “critical, underserved markets.”
Re:Build says its network of companies employs more than 2,100 people in the U.S. and houses more than 2.4 million square feet of manufacturing capacity.

Wilke and his co-founder Miles Arnone came up with the idea of Slate Auto in 2022, and decided to spin it out in order to help it attract more capital. The company has since gone on to raise at least $1.4 billion, including funding from Bezos’ family office, in an attempt to build an ultra low-cost, bare bones pickup truck that can be customized to a customer’s liking.

articles.headline: This Room In Dark Souls Is My Personal Waking Nightmare
keyFacts: The author stated they are revisiting the original Dark Souls and are currently stuck in Anor Londo.
The author said a specific room right before the Ornstein and Smough boss fight causes them extreme frustration.
The author explained that trying to summon Solaire of Astora in that room forces them to fight difficult enemies repeatedly.
body: While waiting patiently for the release of both the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and GTAVI, I’ve been revisiting the original Dark Souls. I’ve never beaten Dark Souls; the first time I played I got as far as defeating Gaping Dragon and then noped out when I hit Blighttown. This time, I’ve stuck it out, and am all the way through most of Anor Londo. Game’s great! What a classic! Mostly!

I love games that are rude in the extreme to the player in comical ways, and this is something FromSoftware excels at doing. God, Dark Souls is such a hilarious asshole to me. Whether it’s crap like this:
Or this:

Funny! I am, quite genuinely laughing about both of those situations. What I am not laughing about, what I am in fact internally and nearly externally screaming about, is a very specific encounter in Anor Londo that has become my own personal house of horrors.

“Ah, yes, Ornstein and Smough,” you say knowingly, recalling the challenging boss duo of Anor Londo. But nay! It’s not them. Even though I am, in fact, currently stuck on them. It’s not Ornstein and Smough who are the issue. In fact, I am confident that I’ll be able to defeat them in a few more good attempts.
No, my trouble, my horror, my agony in Anor Londo is not in that room, but in the room right before them. This room:
Man, fuck this room! It’s so unassuming! So basic! Why am I havingÂ so much trouble with this room?
I know why. It’s a combination of stubbornness and rage that’s tripping me up.Â But also they did not have to make this room so damn frustrating.

To get to Ornstein and Smough from one of the two nearest bonfires, you have to run through several long corridors. One run is mostly empty, but has two big, chonky unavoidable knight enemies at the end before you hit this room, so it’s non-ideal. The other run is peppered with silver knight enemies, but you can outrun all of them easily. The run itself is long, but not too dangerous.

The issue is when you get in here. If you’re not me, and you just want to run through the fog door and fight Ornstein and Smough, you can just do that. But if you’re a stubborn fool, as I am, you want to summon Solaire of Astora to accompany you through the door and fight with you. You want to do this both because he’s badass and a great help at dealing with the otherwise very challenging Ornstein and Smough, but also because he’s cool as hell and it’s fun to team up with story characters for big fights. Yeah! Praise the sun!

Unfortunately, Solaire’s summon sign is all the way on the other side of the room, and there’s no way to activate it without drawing the ire of every enemy in the room. Here, let me show you a diagram:

So the goal is to get from the right-hand side of the church upstairs to the left, head down some stairs, summon Solaire, then head the rest of the way downstairs with him and through the fog gate. Easy, right? Wrong. First, what’s important to know is that basically any attempt to get Solaire through that door without killing all three enemies in the room first will result in Solaire fighting those enemies instead of following you to Ornstein and Smough. Sometimes he’ll fight them for a bit, sustain way too much damage, then follow you. Sometimes he’ll just…stay in here. Forever. Until Smough murders you with his hammer and it’s too late.

The reason Solaire will fight these enemies is because their aggro range is massive. Basically anywhere in that church apart from the very top floor, they will see you and start moving. I have tried all sorts of combinations of pathing to avoid and/or lose their interest, but no dice. Also, it takes several seconds to summon Solaire, so there’s no way to just speed through, quickly grabbing him on the way to the door. Murder it is then.

The archer on the left must be dealt with first, but fortunately he’s pretty easy. He takes two, on a bad run three swings of my big axe to go down, and I can pretty reliably avoid being hit by his arrows if I just sprint at him. No problem.

The issue is the two big guys downstairs. They’re so annoying! They take several good swings to the back to kill: front attacks do nothing against their big shields. They also love to jump backwards or use an annoying spell to push me away, and then heal themselves. Also, sometimes I misread their attack as a spear attack when really they’re slamming their whole shield into the ground, which does a ton of damage in a large radius and usually hits me, knocking me down and forcing me to slowly stumble to my feet again, only to get stabbed with a spear the second I’m up. Agh!

The thing is, they should, on paper, be very easy to kill! I have done it, many times, with zero issue! They are slow, and their hits are very obviously telegraphed. Dodging should be a cinch. And yet. I have now done this run so many times now that I am starting to get in my own head about fighting them, and I keep either losing tons of much-needed Estus flasks and charges of Great Magic Weapon fighting them, or they just wallop me entirely. Or maybe it goes fine. Maybe I get through it with full flasks and health, summon Solaire, and head on into the fight. But God damn, that was so time-consuming. The run by itself is long enough without having to fight one small dude and two big damage sponges at the end. But if you include how long it takes to kill these three guys every single time, especially when they self-heal…ugh.Â Why couldn’t there be just, like, one less big guy in here?

This is it! This room is hell! Those archers back there on the ramparts, the ones everyone complained about? Cake compared to this stupid room! Get me out of this horror show! Forget Halloween, this place lives in my nightmares daily! I’m getting chills just writing about it! I’ll go as a big stompy knight for Halloween this year and scare myself!
No! I will not change my strategy and stop trying to summon the sun bro, what are you talking about?

Also,Â also, I have to burn a Humanity back at the bonfire every time I want to summon Solaire. Sometimes they kill me before I even summon him, and I lose the Humanity. I am now out of Humanities. If I want to do the fight with Solaire at my side, I gotta go farm some more. Easiest way to do that is to run all the way back out of Anor Londo, through Sen’s Fortress, back toâ
GodÂ damn it.

articles.headline: Republicans are coming for your blue M&Ms
keyFacts: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is pressuring food companies to remove synthetic artificial dyes from snacks.
Mars spent millions attempting to create naturally dyed M&Ms, but algae-derived spirulina clogged factory machinery.
Mars released naturally dyed M&Ms in red, orange, yellow, and green, omitting blue and brown due to cost.
body: A close-up image shows a bowl of blue M&M candies. | Peter Macdiarmid/Getty Images
If you were anything like me as a kid, trick-or-treating meant one, maybe two, pillowcases full of candy every Halloween.
And as fun as collecting all that candy could be, the real fun began when I got home and dumped my winnings onto my bedroom floor. That’s when the sorting began.

I had some very specific rules: The usual suspects — think Smarties, Tootsie Rolls, and Dum Dums — went into one pile. Fun-size chocolates, like Snickers, Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups, and Baby Ruths, went into another. And then there was my prized pile: Skittles, Warheads, Starbursts, and Sour Patch Kids. Those were meant to be eaten slowly throughout November. The rest was fair game.

The ways we sort and eat our Halloween candy are decided by some very particular, personal rules. But Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. would like to add another distinction: Which candies are made with artificial dyes?

Kennedy’s ire for synthetic food dyes is years old, and they’ve become a major target of his Make America Healthy Again movement. Last year, he announced a plan to remove “petroleum-based synthetic dyes” from foods, arguing that companies “shouldn’t be feeding it to the rest of us.”

That plan has become a multimillion-dollar problem for Mars, the maker of M&Ms, which promised customers last year that they would create an all-natural version of their tasty chocolatey treats. As the Wall Street Journal reported this summer, however, its latest offering is missing one of the most iconic colored M&Ms — the blue M&M.

M&Ms aren’t the only snack food in Kennedy’s crosshairs: He has called out Doritos, Cheez-Its, Cap’n Crunch, and gummy bears, saying their ingredients include “a lot of poisons.” On Fox News, he described what children eat as “food-like substances” and also said that “some of it was made in petroleum refineries.”

In reality, the evidence is more complicated, because the Food and Drug Administration has long considered many of these approved synthetic dyes to be safe under its rules, while acknowledging that some children may be sensitive to them. Kennedy’s sweeping accusations go much further.

Still, pressure from Kennedy and those in the MAHA movement has led many companies to rethink the recipes of your favorite snacks. But producing those alternatives isn’t easy or cheap, as the story of the blue M&M illustrates.

Jesse Newman , a food reporter for the Wall Street Journal, went inside a Mars factory in Topeka, Kansas, to see the process for herself. She spoke with Today, Explained co-host Noel King about why blue is so difficult to produce naturally, and what changing a candy’s color actually accomplishes.

Below is an excerpt of their conversation, edited for length and clarity. There’s much more in the full podcast, so listen to Today, Explained wherever you get your podcasts, including Apple Podcasts , Pandora , and Spotify .
The Secretary of Health and Human Services, RFK Jr., has some issues with the blue M&M. What, what exactly happened? How did it draw his attention?
He is not a fan of any sort of chemical. He’s really concerned about toxins in our food. And Blue 1, which is the food dye that makes blue M&Ms blue, is a synthetic chemical.
He really takes issue with artificial dyes. He believes that they cause hyperactivity in kids, some neurological challenges. He thinks artificial dyes are linked to cancer.
As a member of the Trump administration, he formally set out to get them removed, didn’t he?
Oh yeah. He’s been putting a lot of pressure on the industry to strip artificial dyes from all kinds of products.

What do we know factually about artificial dyes? We hear that they’re bad for us. We hear that a lot of things are bad for us. We’re all still alive and kicking. Are artificial dyes really detrimental to our health?

The FDA for decades has said that there are nine artificial dyes approved for use in food. And they said that those artificial dyes are safe and have said so for years and years and years, as have other global bodies, so long as they’re used in accordance with some of the standards that the FDA laid out.

A California state agency has found that dyes are linked again to hyperactivity in children. And the FDA itself has said, ‘Okay, we think that these dyes are safe for the vast majority of kids, but some kids might be more sensitive to them than others.’

So I think the real issue is that it’s a chemical doing it. They’re purely cosmetic. They don’t do anything except color food. There is no nutritional benefit that you are getting from these dyes. And so do we need them? Absolutely not.
I think one of the issues is that if you’re looking at the ways our food contributes to health problems, artificial dyes are probably pretty low on the list.
You went inside a factory where they make M&Ms, and you looked at how they’re trying to make this happen. Tell me everything.

I went to this plant in Topeka, Kansas, to see how they were made. And it’s a massive industrial food plant, where they mix these colors and spray them onto these small chocolate orbs, which they refer to as lentils.

The M&Ms move through the plant, and they arrive at these massive [machines] that they call pans, but they look like big tumble dryers. And the M&Ms just tumble around in these pans, and the color is sprayed on. It’s a very, very industrial process, millions of M&Ms a day. And the challenge that Mars has now is making that happen with a natural dye instead of an artificial one.
A blue natural dye is the challenge. What are the problems?
They’ve been working on this for years. And they went with a product called spirulina, which is made from algae. But spirulina comes with a host of problems that they are now dealing with.

Blue 1, which is the artificial dye, arrives at the factories as a liquid. And they pour it into these mixers and they mix it up with this sugary syrup and it’s pretty easy to handle. Spirulina arrives as a powder. So now you’re mixing a powder into this same mixture, into the same recipe, and that is very different.

Because spirulina is a protein, the resulting mixture becomes a lot thicker. What they found was that the mixture containing spirulina would really clog up the piping. It was getting stuck. It moved less smoothly through the pipes.

Also because it is a protein, it was starting to coat and build up on the inside of the machinery. And when that happens, it’s a food safety hazard. It can mold; it can cause problems. For many reasons, it was a challenge to handle.
How much did this all cost?
I should say it’s not done. Mars wouldn’t give me an official figure for how much they spent. But they said that they are spending millions and millions of dollars.

They’re having to retrofit their plants, essentially. Mars said that they’re having to change about 300 types of machinery in their plants. It’s a real investment. And at the end of the day, it all comes down to cost.
What did they actually end up getting done? What was the outcome here?

Mars said what they committed to was that they were going to release a new version of their M&Ms and a few other of their products this year that were made with natural dyes instead of artificial dyes.
They didn’t come out and say we’re eliminating artificial dyes. And so folks should be really clear about that: Their artificially dyed M&Ms aren’t going anywhere. They are still on shelves.

What they said is that they’re going to come out with an option that is naturally dyed. So they tried to do that. And what they found was that they couldn’t do it at a cost that was acceptable to them. With the blue and with the spirulina, it would have been far too expensive to make it work at scale. We’re talking millions and millions and millions of M&Ms per day.

They had problems making the green, the blue, and the brown M&M because, if you go back to your elementary school color theory, they needed blue to make all of those M&Ms. Ultimately they said, “Okay, we can do green. There’s little enough spirulina in the green to make the green M&M.” But blue and brown, they are not able to get there yet due to the amount of spirulina that those colors require.

And so earlier this year, they launched their naturally dyed version of M&Ms with red, orange, yellow, and green M&Ms. And if you take a look at this bag, my colleague referred to these as autumnal. They look very autumnal.
They look sort of muted.
You know, it really isn’t the same. It looks like a mature person’s M&M.

At the end of the day, what are the changes to the M&Ms? Let’s say I go online and get the natural dyed ones. What does that mean for my health? Am I now a healthy and virtuous person if I’m eating the autumnal M&Ms?
It means very little.

I would say you are, hopefully, still enjoying that sugary treat and the pick-me-up in the afternoon as you’re starting to tire. But you’re still eating candy; you’re still eating sugar. It really hasn’t changed very much.

articles.headline: 'You are deluded!': Wayne Rooney's scathing attack on Man United players amid Michael Carrick slump
keyFacts: Manchester United is experiencing an eight-game winless slump, placing manager Michael Carrick under intense pressure and the team low in the standings.
Former player Wayne Rooney criticized the squad on a podcast, stating that the players are failing to put in effort and are letting Carrick down.
Reports indicate that club executives decided to retain Carrick for the short-term because they could not agree on a replacement.
body: Manchester United are stuck in the middle of a horrible slump which has put manager Michael Carrick's position in serious threat.

They have failed to win any of their last eight games across all competitions, dating back to the 4-0 Champions League victory over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah in mid-September. Starting with the defeat in the subsequent Manchester derby, they have lost five and drawn three by a combined score of 16-6, including 7-1 over their last two games.

Heavy losses to Como and Bournemouth over the past week have put the manager's tenure under heavy pressure, with the club sitting 16th in the Premier League table, and 20th in the Champions League standings.

Carrick has not yet been dismissed, and according to one Man United legend, the players are more to blame than the manager is, and the club will continue to flounder if the squad can't get its act together.
MORE: All the latest Man United news
Wayne Rooney says Man United players need a stark reminder

Former Man United star Wayne Rooney is furious with the lack of desire by the players in the current squad, pointing to the recent defeat to Bournemouth as the latest example of what he believes to be poor effort.
"The players haven't got a leg to stand on," Rooney said on the Stick to United podcast which airs on Disney+. "What's not fair is the performances they are giving.

"I looked at the fans, you could see the pain and anger in their faces when those players are walking around the football pitch. You see [Lisandro] Martinez when [Bournemouth forward] Rayan ran round him, they are not getting to the ball, it's so frustrating.

"I could score a goal, had ability or whatever, at least I f***ing ran and put myself about as a team. These players are not doing that. I would love to go in that dressing room and say, 'What the f*** are you all doing? What type of performances do you think this is? Do you think you deserve to wear the shirt?' Put a f***ing firework up their a**** because they are not doing anything.

"We are seeing players who are numb, look like they have got no emotion, look like they don't care. Some of them might care, some good lads who are getting dragged down. It is so frustrating to watch."
Rooney believes that the players have failed to do their part for the team, and therefore are letting the manager down.

"The squad is absolutely a million miles away," Rooney said. "The worst thing for Michael Carrick, he has given the board a bit of hope when in reality, they needed a big overhaul and have done for years.
"The midfield, spending that amount on those midfielders, is absolutely crazy. I feel for Michael, he has being let down, he hasn't been good enough, but the players have let him down massively."

It seems the fans agree with Rooney, at least judging by their cheering and jeering after the Bournemouth defeat on the weekend. The away fans at Vitality Stadium cheered Carrick as he walked down the tunnel, and then began to boo the players once he had disappeared into the underbelly of the stadium.
Emotional exit by Michael Carrick as fans sing his name. A farewell? Supporters turn on players once Carrick down tunnel. #MUFC https://t.co/WLYqqHg6vF
— Laurie Whitwell (@lauriewhitwell) October 25, 2026
Michael Carrick to remain as Man United coach for now
According to multiple reports on Tuesday, Manchester United had elected to stick with Michael Carrick for now, despite recent embarrassing defeats to Como and Bournemouth over the past week.

A report from Samuel Luckhurst of The Sun claimed Man United brass had originally planned to sack Carrick, but couldn't agree on a subsequent move forward to replace him, whether interim or permanently, so they decided to stick it out a bit longer.

On Monday, the club had declined to comment whether Carrick would take charge of training on Tuesday, but decided to keep him on for the short-term. According to Laurie Whitwell of The Athletic, the decision came from co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada, and director of football Jason Wilcox. keyFacts: The Federal Election Commission reported a filing system outage on Tuesday that blocked candidates and political action committees from submitting mandatory finance reports.
According to an email obtained by Reuters, the mishap resulted from a hacking attempt, though the FEC has not publicly disclosed the official cause.
The FEC did not announce when the electronic filing system will be restored or whether any information was compromised.
body: The Federal Election Commission experienced a filing system outage on Tuesday, hindering candidates and political action committees from filing 24- and 48-hour finance reports with a week to go before the midterm elections.

The FEC posted to its status update page shortly before 3 p.m. Tuesday that it is continuing to investigate the outage. According to the commission, the filing system began experiencing issues late Monday evening.
While the system is down for organizations attempting to file spending reports, the FEC website is still working for those tracking spending by candidates and organizations.

The FEC has not disclosed what caused the system outage, but according to an email obtained by Reuters , the mishap is due to a hacking attempt. Hacking attempts are unusual for the FEC, according to Steven Mele, a partner at political finance compliance firm MBA Consulting Group, who spoke with the outlet.

The disruption comes at a particularly consequential time for campaign finance disclosures, with candidates and outside political groups pouring money into competitive races ahead of the Nov. 3 elections . While the filing system outage will not affect voters casting their ballots, it will affect their ability to see updated financial reports from the candidates they are weighing.

Under FEC regulations, PACs and other organizations making independent expenditures are required to submit reports disclosing certain spending within 24 or 48 hours, depending on the amount spent and the proximity to Election Day.

During the final 19 days before an election, independent expenditures totaling $1,000 or more in a particular race trigger a 24-hour reporting requirement . Earlier in the election cycle, expenditures reaching $10,000 generally trigger a 48-hour reporting requirement.

The disclosures provide a window into last-minute political spending, including how much outside groups are spending to support or oppose candidates and which races are attracting financial attention.
The FEC did not make clear when the electronic filing system would be restored or whether any information had been compromised in the reported hacking attempt.

articles.headline: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
keyFacts: A humanitarian ceasefire initiated in Russian-occupied Oleshky was extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials said.
Melania Trump and Pope Leo XIV helped broker the truce to assist thousands of trapped residents, officials said.
The ceasefire enables humanitarian aid deliveries to Oleshky followed by resident evacuations planned for Friday, officials said.
body: - Published
A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources.

Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity. On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous.
However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported.
US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.

That was later corroborated by the press secretary to Ukraine's public ombudsman, and by Oleksandr Tolokonnikov, deputy head of Kherson, who said Russian shelling had stopped both in Kherson city, which is in Ukrainian hands, and the wider region.
Under the deal, the ceasefire will be followed by deliveries of humanitarian aid to Oleshky and then evacuations, planned for Friday, for anyone wishing to leave.
An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 people remain in Oleshky itself and a few thousand more in surrounding areas.
Many residents have resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive, telling the BBC they are suffering extreme hunger and want to leave.

Both sides said the ceasefire was being observed. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said everything was proceeding "according to plan", and paid tribute to US mediation and in particular representatives of Melania Trump.
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said if the ceasefire produced results, it could "pave the way for other steps in the peace process".

A key official in President Volodymyr Zelensky's parliamentary party, David Arakhamia, said it would continue until 22:59 Ukrainian time on Sunday 1 November, and described the truce as the "largest de-escalation since 2022".
Before the war Oleshky was home to 24,000 people, but it was seized by Russia during the first days of its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
No shops are open, and the city has had no electricity, gas or water since the Kakhovka Dam was blown up in 2023, flooding the area and killing many people in Oleshky itself.

Conditions have become so desperate that not only is getting supplies into the city extremely difficult, but escaping is too risky because the routes out of Oleshky have been mined and subject to drone attack.

One woman told the BBC she had stepped on a landmine and was currently in hospital where she had undergone two operations: "I don't know how long I will have to spend there," she said, worried about not being able to join the evacuation.

Pope Leo appealed earlier this month to Russia's President Vladimir Putin to allow food and medical aid into Oleshky as well as a safe evacuation, and urged his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky to co-operate with Moscow over a ceasefire.
Then the White House said last week that Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire.
On Tuesday, the US first lady said on X that the area covered by the ceasefire "has expanded beyond Oleshky, within the Kherson region, to provide safe passage for the humanitarian convoys".

The current truce is supposed to enable roads to be cleared of mines for supplies to get into the city possibly on Thursday, and for residents to have safe passage out in an evacuation planned for Friday.

Russia's defence ministry said units from the army's Dnepr group had been conducting "engineering reconnaissance" and clearing main access roads into the village of "explosive and booby-trap devices".

Many details on the evacuation plans are unclear, and residents are wary of trusting officials with their names and addresses. However, a local volunteer told the BBC that about 500 people had already expressed interest by Tuesday afternoon.

Vladimir Saldo, the Russian-installed head of occupied areas of Kherson, said temporary accommodation had been prepared in the region itself as well as Russian-annexed Crimea and across the Russian border in the Rostov, Krasnodar and Stavropol regions.
Saldo told Russian media that most Oleshky residents wanted to leave the city and stay in Russia, although his account has not been corroborated on the ground.
It is hard to make contact with people there as communication is patchy and many are reluctant to speak of the situation in fear of reprisals from the Russians.

Those residents or relatives who have spoken to the BBC have expressed fears that Russia may not allow them to return to Ukraine, or might examine their phones and online activity for signs of Ukrainian support, which could put them in danger.
Ukraine's military general staff urged people not to trust unverified reports or spread rumours about "the routes, time and place of the movement of people and humanitarian convoys".
Zelensky has warned that routes out of Oleshky that are demined by Russia will ensure that those civilians leaving Oleshky will "head towards Russia and stay there".
He said some residents would get to Ukrainian-controlled territory "one way or another", and that ideally anyone trapped would be able to reach their destination and evacuate to Ukraine.

One resident called Serhii, who fled Oleshky through minefields around three weeks ago, said he had eventually returned to Ukraine via Russia and Belarus. He called for a route across the River Dnipro that avoided Russian-occupied territory, saying "you simply cannot trust the Russian Federation".
However, bridges across the River Dnipro have been destroyed and sources say the riverbank is also mined and dangerous, so crossing into Ukrainian-controlled territory appears impossible.

Across the river, in Kherson city, no explosions have been heard and no drone-related injuries reported since 03:00 (01:00 GMT) on Tuesday and cars and pedestrians have been moving freely, according to local reports.
"Judging from the fact that more people are walking around, it feels a bit calmer," Galina Kyrychenko, a resident in the city, told public broadcaster Suspilne.
Additional reporting by Anastasiia Levchenko in Kyiv.

The stark rise in gas and diesel prices, a product of Iran’s closure of the Strait of Hormuz in the war’s opening days, has been a major source of grievance against Republicans going into the 2024 midterms.

At a campaign stop in Michigan, JD Vance further escalated a war of words he’s exchanged with the state’s Democratic Senate candidate, Abdul El-Sayed.

Speaking to the crowd in Howell, Michigan, Vance sought to connect El-Sayed’s politics to the left-wing protests in Paris that have led to thousands of arrests – what Vance described as “hordes of masked rioters, many from distant lands, taking over historic city centers.”
He also continued to play up El-Sayed’s relationship with left-wing political commentator Hasan Piker.

“The scene of destruction in Paris may be an ocean away, but ask yourselves, are they really so hard to imagine here in the United States of America?” Vance said. “And I guarantee you, if those rioters were burning down New York, or Detroit, the Hasan Pikers and El-Sayeds would be right there leading them and cheering them on.”
He continued: “What we saw in France, the hatred, the ingratitude, the desire to destroy rather than the desire to build, that exact same cancer is what has corrupted Abdul El-Sayed.”
Vance has made several visits to Michigan as Republicans seek to win the seat El-Sayed is vying for, leading the two to exchange barbs at campaign rallies and on social media.
Trump administration boat strikes continue with attack in Eastern Pacific
Another US strike on a purported drug-smuggling vessel in the eastern Pacific on Tuesday killed 5 people, according to the US military.

The strikes is just the latest in dozens of similar attacks in the Caribbean and Pacific that have killed more than 240 people, and that the Trump administration has claimed are targeting drug traffickers, branded “narcoterrorists” by the president. But they’ve been widely criticized as illegal extrajudicial killings, and the administration has not furnished evidence that all of those killed are connected to the drug trade.
DoJ asks Washington state not to count ballots from possible noncitizens

The US justice department has asked Washington statenot to count any mail ballots received from more than 400 residents who it says may not be US citizens, Reuters reports, opening a new front in the Trump administration’s push to expand control of election administration ahead of next Tuesday’s midterms.

The letter, which resembled a request earlier this month that California not count any ballots received from around 20,000 alleged noncitizens, marked an escalation in the Trump administration’s pressure on state election officials over alleged noncitizen voting.
Multiple state audits and independent studies have found that voter fraud, including voting by noncitizens, is extremely rare and has not affected election outcomes.

The pressure campaign is a rare intervention by the Justice Department in the voting process in the weeks before an election. Donald Trump’s Republican party is locked in a tight battle to retain slim majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, and centrist Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez’s campaign to hold onto her southwest Washington seat is one of 10 key races that could decide control of the US House of Representatives.

In the letter, dated 26 October, the top federal prosecutors in Seattle and Spokane asked Washington secretary of state Steve Hobbs, the state’s top elections official, to determine whether the more than 400 people were in fact US citizens and to not count their ballots until their citizenship was determined. The letter said the justice department would seek “emergency relief” if the state could not take those actions by noon local time tomorrow.
There were 5 million registered voters in Washington state as of 2024, according to the secretary of state’s office.
In a statement, Hobbs said his office would only respond to requests that follow due process.
“The timing of this request — one week before the General Election — is no doubt intended to cast unfounded suspicion on the results,” Hobbs said.
A justice department spokesperson said: “With his [Hobbs’] help, we can ensure that only American citizens vote in Washington’s elections.“
In its letter to Washington state officials, the justice department acknowledged that some of the individuals flagged as possible noncitizens may have since naturalized, but it did not say how many.

Federal law enforcement agents searched a home in suburban Los Angeles early today as part of an investigation into Eric Swalwell, who resigned from Congress amid a wave of sexual misconduct allegations, a law enforcement official and two people familiar with the investigation told the Associated Press.

Agents searched the Beverly Hills home of wealthy developer and Swalwell donor Stephen Cloobeck, where the Democratic ex-congressman spent time before resigning from office in April, according to the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss the investigation.
Swalwell has denied criminal wrongdoing.
Messages seeking comment were left for Swalwell’s attorney and for a lawyer who represented Cloobeck in another matter.
Cloobeck, the founder of the Diamond Resorts International timeshare company, told the New York Post in April that he cut ties with Swalwell as accusations against him mounted.
“I am no longer associated with a man that takes advantage of women,” Cloobeck told the newspaper. “I support women’s rights.”

Today’s search is the latest escalation in the federal investigation of Swalwell – one of several probes begun after a woman came forward with allegations that he sexually assaulted her twice, including when she worked for him.

The San Francisco Chronicle, followed by CNN, first reported the allegations. CNN also reported that three other women alleged various kinds of sexual misconduct by Swalwell, including sending them unsolicited explicit messages or nude photos.
Trump’s cuts have exposed US to ‘cascade’ of El Niño dangers, experts warn
Gabrielle Canon

Sweeping cuts to the premier US climate agency under Donald Trump have severely hampered the country’s capacity to forecast,research and respond to extreme weather events, former government officials and scientists have warned, as the US faces a cascade of hazards fueled by a potentially historic El Niño this winter.

From the start of his second term, the president has taken aim at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa), slashing staff levels, canceling contracts and grants, and shutting down databases and research laboratories. The agency that has long been considered a global crown jewel in climate science and forecasting, has lost roughly 20% of its staff since January 2025.

The National Weather Service, which is housed within Noaa, has also taken a hit. Weather stations have had to delay data collection and cut operating hours, with hundreds of meteorological and other technical positions still vacant across its 122 forecast offices.

The effects have already been felt at Noaa, where a chaotic and volatile environment has sent morale plummeting, increased burnout and hampered vital work. While capacity has quietly unravelled, a large-scale disaster will quickly expose the most dangerous gaps.
“The system has not really been tested since all the cuts happened,” said Tom Di Liberto, a former Noaa climate scientist who now works as the media director of Climate Central.
That test could soon be coming.

This year’s super El Niño, a climate phenomenon characterized by warmer than average equatorial sea surface temperatures, has the ability to fuel extreme weather events around the world. It’s already climbing off the charts and is expected to strengthen through the northern hemisphere’s autumn and winter.

Along with dangerous spikes in temperature, El Niño will supercharge storms in parts of the American west, raise sea levels in California by up to a foot, and set the stage for debris flows, landslides and flash floods.
“Whether we as a country can handle the kind of coast-to-coast extremes that could potentially happen this winter is a big question,” Di Liberto said.

In the latest episode of our Stateside podcast, Carter Sherman speaks to Julian Borger, the Guardian’s senior international correspondent, about how historic elections in Serbia, Brazil, Israel and the United States could reshape the political world order in just 10 days - and why the upcoming US midterm elections are the biggest test for global democracy.
Trump refers to oil tanker he'll show off in Texas as a personal "gift" from Venezuela

Before heading to Texas, Trump spoke in blunt terms about the US’s relationship with Venezuela, describing a massive shipment of oil he’ll show off at a campaign stop as a personal gift from a subdued country.
“We took over Venezuela, very successfully,” Trump said. “And they’ve sent me as a gift, a boatload of a million barrels of oil, and I’m giving that to the United States of America.”

The Trump administration deposed Venezuela’s former leader, Nicólas Maduro, in January, dragging the autocrat off to a Brooklyn jail after a nighttime incursion into the Venezuelan capital of Caracas. His US-friendly successor, Delcy Rodriguez, who took power with Trump’s backing, has since brokered deals with the Trump administration that would see Venezuela oil revenues funneled into US coffers.
The oil shipment from Venezuela is part of Trump’s efforts to tamp down voters’ outrage over soaring gas prices due to the war in Iran.
“We’re going to accept a million barrels of oil, and I’m going to give it to you people to use it the way you want,” Trump said.“Oil prices are going to be dropping very sharply, very soon.”

Pressed on the tarmac en route to a pair of Texas campaign events on whether he would accept the election results of the 2026 midterm elections, President Trump gave a familiar reply: “I will, if they’re honest.”
He also said he would be open to working with, and potentially making deals, with a Democratic majority if Republicans were to lose control of Congress.
“I hope that won’t be the case, but if it is, that’s happened before with many presidents,” Trump told reporters. “You have strong veto, and you end up working out deals.”
Trump-appointed CDC deputy director to resign after six months on the job
Jessica Glenza
The deputy director and chief medical officer of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) will resign after six months on the job, according to an agency email obtained by the Guardian.
Dr Jennifer Shuford was appointed by Donald Trump in April as part of a four-person senior leadership team.

The appointments were meant to stabilize the agency after the previous CDC director, Susan Monarez, left less than a month into the job – publicly describing the directives of the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, as “unscientific”.

“I am leaving to spend more time with my family,” Shuford said in a statement, sent via email by the CDC director, Dr Erica Schwartz. “I am so thankful to President Trump and Secretary Kennedy for giving me the opportunity to help lead CDC. It has been an amazing experience, and I will be forever grateful for it.”
Shuford is expected to leave her post on 12 November, after the midterm elections.

The deputy director was appointed as part of a four-person team in April, alongside Schwartz and two other top leaders. Shuford’s appointment was cheered by public health leaders, such as Association of State and Territorial Health Officials (ASTHO), who would have known her work as Texas health commissioner.

In the time since Shuford has worked at the agency, Kennedy has made significant changes that undermine vaccine trust and access. In just a few recent examples: Kennedy fired all 17 of the CDC’s expert vaccine advisory panel members and replaced them with ideologically aligned appointees, slow-walked death updates to the agency’s measles dashboard, and forced the CDC to publicly contradict scientific consensus on vaccines and autism – a change the Autism Science Foundation said left it “appalled”.

At the same time, the agency has lost one-third of its workforce and 48 distinct measles outbreaks have roiled the US, particularly in Pennsylvania. The overwhelming majority of Americans – including Maha supporters – trust vaccines.
Tom Phillips, chief justice of Texas supreme court, endorses James Talarico in Senate race
Tom Phillips, a longtime chief justice of the Texas Supreme Court and a staunch Republican, endorsed Democrat James Talarico in the Texas Senate race on Monday.

In an op-ed published in the Austin American-Statesman, Phillips, a Republican who served as the state’s chief justice from 1988 to 2004, said that he believed that Talarico would be a better representative of Texas in the Senate, and more willing to engage in productive bipartisanship.

By contrast, he said, Paxton would be a Trump acolyte who would enable the president’s excesses and self-dealing, steering the Republican Party away from the ideals Phillips believes it should embody, such as limited government and free enterprise.
He also felt that Paxton’s history of scandal would cast a shadow over his Senate tenure, regardless of his future conduct.

“However exemplary his future conduct might be, Paxton’s longstanding reputation will embarrass Texas in ways our state simply cannot afford,” Phillips wrote. “While I, like many Republicans, do not agree with all of Talarico’s past statements or current positions, I am confident that he would serve this great state with dignity and honor.”
Phillips said he believed there were still Republican candidates on the ticket who were worthy of serving. Paxton just wasn’t one of them.

“Thus, while I enthusiastically support the statewide Republican judicial candidates and many Republican candidates for other statewide offices, my choice for United States Senator must be James Talarico,” Phillips wrote.

Intel processors, AI capabilities, and enterprise security

body: World of Warcraft: Forever's character creation and name reservations are now live, letting you save some time on launch day by making your characters now rather than on launch day.

To access name reservations, you'll need to have Forever preinstalled on Battle.net and have purchased at least the $30 Skyborne Heroic Pack , which grants access to the game's new optional playable race, the Skyborne elves.
